title: Best Network Access Control (NAC) Solutions: Our Top Picks by Use Case (2026)
content_md: Network access control decides which devices are allowed onto your network and what they can reach once connected. The right NAC platform depends far more on what you’re trying to control than on which vendor tops a market-share chart a hospital with 12,000 unmanaged medical devices needs something completely different from a 200-person company that wants contractors off the finance VLAN. We evaluated eight leading NAC platforms from the top cybersecurity companies and matched each to the buyer it genuinely serves. Best NAC by Use Case — At a Glance Your situation Our pick Score Heavy IoT / OT / medical devices Forescout 8.8 Large enterprise, Cisco network Cisco ISE 8.6 Wireless-first campus (education, healthcare) HPE Aruba ClearPass 8.5 Mid-market wanting cloud simplicity OPSWAT MetaAccess 7.9 Existing Extreme network estate Extreme Networks 7.7 Endpoint-management-led IT team Ivanti 7.5 Cloud-first SMB or mid-market seeking SaaS NAC Portnox 8.6 SMB or mid-sized enterprise needing affordable multi-vendor NAC macmon NAC 7.8 Definitional answer: network access control (NAC) authenticates and profiles every device attempting to join a network, checks it against policy patch level, certificate, ownership, device type and then permits, restricts, or quarantines it. Modern NAC extends beyond 802.1X to agentless profiling for devices that can’t authenticate themselves.
